They are currently competing under the name '''Dplus Kia''' due to a title sponsorship with '''Kia'''. {{cite web|url=https://esportsinsider.com/2020/12/damwon-kia-naming-sponsor|title=DAMWON Gaming partners with Kia Motors, renames to DWG KIA|author=Billy Studholme|publisher=Esports Insider|date=2020-12-22}} (Originally renaming from DAMWON Gaming to DWG Kia before their rebrand to Dplus). Dplus is one of the organizations that has won a World Championship by winning in [[World_Championship/2020|2020]] when they were called DAMWON Gaming. {{SectionLinks |rosterHeader=Player Roster |achievementsHeader=Results |historyHeader=History |mediaHeader=Media }} ==Player Roster== {{box|start|padding=2em}} ===Active=== {{ActiveSquadAuto}} {{box|break|padding=2em}} ==={{team|damwon gaming challengers}}=== {{LPDB storage|false}} {{ActiveSquadAuto|team=damwon gaming challengers}} {{LPDB storage|true}} {{box|end|padding=2em}} ===Timeline=== {{TimelineSquadAuto |{{SquadAutoRow|date=2023-01-09|displaydate=January 9th|text=DAMWON Gaming rebrand to [[Dplus]]. }} |{{SquadAutoRow|date=2026-02-25 |displaydate=February 25th |text={{player|Lucid|pos=jgl}}'s contract is extended, expiring at the end of 2027. {{cite web |url=https://x.com/DplusKia/status/2026585787962372477 |title=We have re-signed with Lucid! |publisher=[[Dplus]] |date=2026-02-25}}}} }} ===Former=== {{FormerSquadAuto |{{SquadAutoRow|id=Boroona|name=Kim Yeong-hoon|joindate=2017-05-28}} |{{SquadAutoRow|id=CooN|name=Park Jae-ha|joindate=2017-07-09}} }} ==Organization== ===Active=== {{ActiveOrganizationAuto |{{SquadAutoRow|id=|flag=kr|name=Lee Yu-young|role=Owner|joindate=}} |{{SquadAutoRow|id=|flag=kr|name=Lee Jun-young|role=COO|joindate=}} }} ===Former=== {{FormerOrganizationAuto |{{SquadAutoRow|id=GalBi|name=Lee Ju-hyeob|joindate=2018-06-13}} |{{SquadAutoRow|id=MorNinG|name=Song Chang-geun|joindate=2018-11-26}} |{{SquadAutoRow|id=Jay|link=Jay_(Lee_Jang-hee)|flag=kr|name=Lee Jang-hee|joindate=2022-11-30}} }} ==Results== {{Tabs dynamic|hide-showall=true |name1=Achievements |content1={{Team achievements table|team=DAMWON Gaming}} |name2=Recent Matches |content2={{Team recent matches table|team=DAMWON Gaming}} }} ==Awards== {{Team awards table|team=DAMWON Gaming}} ==History== In 2017, DAMWON Gaming acquired [[MiRaGe Gaming]]'s [[CK/2017/Summer|CK Summer 2017]] slot. They revealed a roster of [[Parang]], [[Crush]], [[Boroona]], [[BeryL]] and [[Hoit]], which would be their starting line-up heading into the season. Halfway through the season, [[CooN]] also joined the team to finish the line-up for this split. Their debut season would end up in 5th place, with a balanced 7/-/7 scoreline in the regular season. This resulted in changes heading into the [[KeSPA_Cup/2017|2017 KeSPA Cup]], with [[Nuguri]] and [[ShowMaker]] joining the starting line-up, while [[Alive]] replaced [[BeryL]] as starting ADC. The team went on to beat [[Kongdoo Monster]], before losing against [[Jin Air Green Wings]] to place 9-12th. In [[CK/2018/Spring|Spring 2018]], [[BeryL]] would return to the starting roster as a support player. The rest of the roster stayed the same, and despite the team making playoffs this time, they still placed 4-5th following a loss against [[Ever8 Winners]]. In [[CK/2018/Summer|Summer 2018]], [[Nuclear]] joined the team as the new starting AD Carry, while [[Punch_(Korean_player)|Punch]] would take on the jungle position. These changes were crucial steps in the team's road to the [[LCK]], with them securing the [[CK/2018/Summer|CK 2018 Summer]] championship and a spot in the [[LCK/2019/Spring/Promotion|LCK 2019 Spring Promotion Tournament]]. With wins against [[bbq Olivers]] and [[Team BattleComics]], DAMWON Gaming finally made it to the LCK. [[DAMWON Gaming|DAMWON]]'s LCK debut started in the [[LCK/2019/Spring|LCK 2019 Spring Split]], with [[Canyon]] joining the team to complete the 5 man roster of [[Nuguri]], [[Canyon]], [[ShowMaker]], [[Nuclear]] and [[BeryL]]. They eventually placed 4th following a playoffs loss against [[KING-ZONE DragonX]]. Resuming with the same roster in [[LCK/2019/Summer|Summer]], DAMWON Gaming placed third and qualified for the [[LCK/2019/Regional_Finals|regional finals]]. This is where they beat [[KING-ZONE DragonX]] 3-2 in the finals, securing them a slot to worlds in their debut year. At [[World_Championship/2019|Worlds 2019]], DAMWON Gaming finished in the quarter finals following a loss against tournament runner-ups [[G2 Esports]]. DAMWON Gaming kept the same roster heading into 2020, and placed 4th in the [[LCK/2020/Spring|2020 Spring Split]]. In [[LCK/2020/Summer|Summer 2020]], DAMWON Gaming won their first [[LCK]] title and secured a direct qualification to [[World_Championship/2020|Worlds 2020]]. They managed to drop just 3 games in the entire tournament, going 5-1 in groups, beating [[DRX]] 3-0, [[G2 Esports]] 3-1, and eventually [[Suning]] 3-1 to secure themselves the 2020 World Championship title. Heading into 2021, [[Khan]] joined the team as a replacement for [[Nuguri]], who left for [[FunPlus Phoenix]] at the end of the 2020 season. With this new 5-man roster, DAMWON Gaming managed to win the [[KeSPA_Cup/2020|2020 KeSPA Cup]], [[LCK/2021/Spring|LCK 2021 Spring Split]] and [[LCK/2021/Summer|LCK 2021 Summer Split]], with a second place at [[Mid-Season_Invitational/2021|MSI 2021]]. With these results, the team secured a direct invite to [[World_Championship/2021|Worlds 2021]] where they are looking to reclaim their title of the world's best. DAMWON Gaming went undefeated in their group, beating [[Cloud9]], [[Rogue]] and [[FunPlus Phoenix]] twice. After wins in against [[MAD Lions]] and [[T1]], they faced off against [[EDward Gaming]], they lost the grand finals in a 5-game fashion, failing to defend their world championship title. In the offseason ahead of 2022, DAMWON Gaming announced that [[Khan]] would retire, later on becoming a streamer for the organisation. [[Burdol]] and [[Hoya]] would become the new toplaners for the team, while [[Ghost (Korean player)|Ghost]] and [[BeryL]] left the team. Replacing them are [[Nongshim RedForce]] botlane duo [[deokdam]] and [[Kellin]]. The team would place 3rd in the [[LCK/2022/Spring|2022 LCK Spring split]], losing against [[Gen.G Esports]]. Ahead of summer, [[Nuguri]] returned to the team. DAMWON Gaming rebranded to [[Dplus]] ahead of the 2023 season. {{cite web |url=https://twitter.com/korizonesports/status/1612346685510004739 |title=[Official] DWG KIA rebrands to Dplus KIA. |date=2023-01-09 |author=[[Korizon]] |publisher=Twitter |language={{Flag|usuk}} English}} ==Gallery== ===Logos=== {{TeamLogoGallery}} ===Rosters=== Dplus Worlds 2024.jpg|Dplus at [[World Championship/2024|Worlds 2024]]

table|team=Fnatic|sdate=2020-01-01}} ==History== Even though '''Fnatic''' was founded in 2004 by Sam Matthews, their journey in League of Legends started in 2011, when the organization acquired the [[MyRevenge]] team roster. {{cite web|url=https://fnatic.com/esports/league-of-legends|title=ACQUISITION OF MYREVENGE|author=Fnatic|publisher=fnatic.com|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}} Initially competing online, the team made their LAN debut as they attended ''League of Legends'' first ever [[World_Championship/2011|World Championship]] in 2011. Although the team started off rough with a 1-2 record in the Group Stage, they made their win through the Winners bracket, and eventually defeated [[against All authority]] in the Grand Finals. Marking their status as the inaugural League of Legends World Champions. The roster, featuring players like [[Shushei]], [[CyanideFI]], [[xPeke]], [[LaMiaZealot]], [[Mellisan]], and [[wewillfailer]], set the foundation for their legacy. Fnatic continued their dominance in the European competitive scene, winning multiple LCS championships and consistently delivering strong performances on the international stage. The team encountered challenges of the competitive League of Legends landscape, with standout moments. While they reached the [[World_Championship/2018|2018 World Championship]] finals, they ultimately fell short against [[Invictus Gaming]]. Fnatic experienced changes in their roster and a spirited rivalry with [[G2 Esports]]. Despite occasional setbacks, Fnatic finished in the top 8 at the [[World_Championship/2020|2020 World Championship]]. The departure of [[Rekkles]] in 2020 marked a significant transition, resulting in the introduction of new talent like [[Upset]] and [[Nisqy]]. The 2021 season brought its own set of challenges, with Fnatic navigating through roster adjustments and internal issues, ultimately leading to a disappointing performance at the [[World_Championship/2021|2021 World Championship]]. This triggered a significant change of their lineup, which included the addition of [[Razork]], [[Wunder]], and [[Humanoid]] for the 2022 season. In 2022, the team secured a spot at the World Championship but concluded their journey in the group stage. As the 2023 season approached, Fnatic continued to make roster changes, with the return of [[Rekkles]] to the AD Carry position. The team faced a variable performance in the [[LEC/2023/Winter|LEC Winter Split 2023]] and made further adjustments, introducing new players and a coaching change. This same roster was invited to [[Intel_Extreme_Masters/Season_VIII/Sao_Paulo|IEM São Paulo]], where they would compete under ocelote's own brand, oceloteWorld. However, on February 24th, 2014 ocelote officially revealed the organization he founded as '''Gamers2''' alongside co-owner Jens Hilgers. {{cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140228073756/http://www.gamers2.com:80/|title=Gamers2 - Press Release|publisher=Gamers2|language={{Flag|usuk}} English|date=2014-02-24}}{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7Fycnq4-QzA|title=Gamers2 - Release Teaser|author=Gamers2|language={{Flag|usuk}} English|date=2014-02-25}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/esports/story/_/id/26806177/g2-grand-vision-targets-more-just-esports-dominance|title=G2's grand vision targets more than just esports dominance|author=Adel Chouadria|publisher=ESPN|language={{Flag|usuk}} English|date=2019-05-24}} The organization started their journey in the [[CS/Europe/2014/Spring/Series_2|European Challenger Series]]. Early on Gamers2 was already commited, even setting up its first headquarters in Spain revealed as the Gamers2 Mansion. {{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YN3N5EPTt3A|title=Gamers2 Mansion - Ocelote Tour!|author=Gamers2|language={{Flag|usuk}} English|date=2014-06-13}} However despite various third place finishes across the Challenger Series, they were unable to make it into the [[CS/Europe/2014/Summer|promotion]] tournament. That year they did gain another chance to make it into the EU LCS through an additional [[LCS/Europe/2015/Spring/Expansion|Expansion]] tournament. However after a loss against [[n!faculty]] in the online stage they were eliminated, and would need to continue in the challenger series. ===Building Up to the EU LCS (2015)=== At the start of 2015, ocelote officially announced his retirement as a player. Meaning he would step back and instead focus on his position as the CEO of Gamers2. {{cite web|url=https://www.reddit.com/r/leagueoflegends/comments/2w2y1k/ocelote_officially_retires/|title=Ocelote officially retires|author=Modifyy|language={{Flag|usuk}} English|date=2015-02-16}}{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/iy_-UOTtfIk|title='Reflections' with ocelote|author=Thorin|language={{Flag|usuk}} English|date=2015-02-16}} While Gamers2 had dabbled in various tournaments with different players in the months, Gamers2 announced that they had acquired [[Team Nevo]]]'s roster the day after ocelote's retirement as their team for the [[CS/Europe/2015/Spring|Challenger Series]]. {{cite web|url=https://x.com/G2esports/status/567792436651773953|title=We are pleased to announce that we have signed @TeamNevo's LoL team.|author=Gamers2|language={{Flag|usuk}} English|date=2015-02-16}} The roster consited of Lennart "[[SmittyJ]]" Warkus, Erberk "[[Gilius]]" Demir, Jérémy "[[Eika]]" Valdenaire, Mohammad "[[Jebus]]" Tokhi, and Aleksi "[[Hiiva]]" Kaikkonen. While they placed in third during the regular season, they lost to [[LowLandLions.White]] 0-2 in their opening match in the playoffs, and would find another loss against [[Reason Gaming]] meaning they lost out on attending the promotion tournament. Over the course of the [[CS/Europe/2015/Summer|Summer]] Split, Gamers2 made various roster changes, ultimately ending their split in third, now heading into the [[LCS/Europe/2016/Spring/Promotion|Promotion tournament]] with their final additions in Mateusz "[[Kikis]]" Szkudlarek, Luka "[[Perkz]]" Perković, Jesse "[[Jesse]]" Le, and Glenn "[[Hybrid]]" Doornenbal. They now had to face [[SK Gaming]] as their final opponent to make it into the [[EU LCS]]. It was also for this match that the team had requested ocelote to join in as their coach. {{cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305014522/http://www.dailydot.com/esports/ocelote-gamers2-lcs-csgo/|title=Ocelote on Gamers2 rebranding plans and how he's building 'a world class esports club'|author=Josh Raven|publisher=Dot Esports|language={{Flag|usuk}} English|date=2015-09-29}}Following a best-of-five series that would go the full lenght, Gamers2 came out on top. Meaning that CEO ocelote had now eliminated the organization he previously played for to make it into the main European League. ===Gamers2 Becomes G2 Esports with Success (2016-2017)=== Heading into the 2016 season, Gamers2 started off with a rebrand as they renamed themselves to '''G2 Esports''' alongside revamping their logo. They would also revamp their roster, moving Kikis to the Top lane, and signing two Korean players in Kim "[[Trick]]" Gang-yun and Kim "[[Emperor]]" Jin-hyun to fill the Jungle and AD Carry position respectively. Finalizing their roster as Joey "[[YoungBuck]]" Steltenpool was appointed as the teams Head Coach. {{cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151230194443/http://www.g2esports.com/g2-agrees-terms-with-emperor-and-trick/|title=G2 agrees terms with Emperor & Trick|author=|publisher=G2 Esports|language={{Flag|usuk}} English|date=2015-12-30}} ==Gallery== ===Logos=== {{TeamLogoGallery}} ===Rosters=== G2 MSI 2019.jpg|G2 Esports at [[Mid-Season_Invitational/2019|MSI 2019]].

Galaxy and the creation of Gen.G Esports (2018)=== On November 30th, 2017, Samsung sold its Esports division, which included the ''League of Legends'' [[World_Championship/2017|2017 World Championship]] roster, [[:leagueoflegends:Samsung Galaxy|Samsung Galaxy]] to Silicon Valley-based esports firm '''{{abbr|KSV|Korea + Silicon Valley}}''' which was founded earlier in the year by Kevin Chou and Kent Wakeford, co-founders of the video game development company Kabam, Michael Li, and Phillip Hyun. {{cite web|url=https://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20171201000733|title=Samsung sells off eSports team to KSV|author=Shin Ji-hye|publisher=The Korea Herald|date=2017-12-01|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}} They participated in the [[LCK/2018/Spring|LCK 2018 Spring]] Split but were eliminated in the playoffs after falling 1-2 against [[SK Telecom T1]]. Following the split, they announced their rebranding in May, changing their name from KSV to '''Gen.G Esports'''. {{cite web|url=https://venturebeat.com/esports/ksv-esports-rebrands-as-gen-g-adds-clash-royale-team/|title=KSV Esports rebrands as Gen.G, adds Clash Royale team|author=Dean Takahashi|publisher=VentureBeat|date=2018-05-03|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}} Heading into [[LCK/2018/Summer|Summer]] Gen.G also added Moon "[[Mong]]" Chang-min, and Song "[[Fly_(Song_Yong-jun)|Fly]]" Yong-jun to their roster for the regular season. {{cite web|url=https://www.invenglobal.com/lol/articles/5085/geng-esports-lol-team-announces-their-new-recruits-fly-and-mong|title=GenG Esports LoL team announces their new recruits: Fly and Mong|author=Byungho "Haao" Kim|publisher=Inven Global|date=2018-05-17|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}} This time the team ended in 4th in the regular season, but saw a prompt exit after losing to the [[Afreeca Freecs]]. With their elimination, they now thad to go through the [[LCK/2018/Regional_Finals|Regional Finals]] as a last chance to go to [[Worlds 2018|Worlds]]. Starting off in the first round as the third seed, they were able to battle their way through, defating the likes of [[SK Telecom T1|SKT]], [[Griffin]] and [[KING-ZONE DragonX|DragonX]] to qualify as the last Korean representative. Their run at Worlds however would be dissapointing one. Falling way behind in the expectations had of the [[LCK]], the team was eliminated in the group stage, ending last in their group with a 1-5 record. To conclude the year, they would part ways with a large part of their roster as [[Ambition]], [[Haru]], [[Crown]], [[CoreJJ]], and [[Mong]] all took their leave, marking an end to the roster that won Worlds in 2017.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/GenG_KR/status/1063242158801473536|title=Farewell, Ambition and Crown|author=Gen.G Esports|date=2018-11-16|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}}{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/100063473119865/posts/1063588377147504/|title=Our contracts with CoreJJ, Haru, & Mong have come to an end.|author=Gen.G Esports|date=2018-11-17|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}} ===(2019)=== The 2019 season saw Gen.G finishing in 7th place in [[LCK/2019/Spring|LCK Spring]] and 6th in [[LCK/2019/Summer|LCK Summer]], failing to qualify for [[World_Championship/2019|Worlds]]. In the 2020 season, they finished 2nd in [[LCK/2020/Spring|LCK Spring]] and reached the playoff stage of the Mid-Season Cup. They ended 3rd in [[LCK/2020/Summer|LCK Summer]] and secured a spot in [[World_Championship/2020|Worlds]] as the 3rd seed via the LCK 2020 Regional Finals. They reached the quarter-finals, but ended up losing to [[G2 Esports]]. ===(2021)=== In 2021, Gen.G finished 2nd in [[LCK/2021/Spring|LCK Spring]] but did not qualify for [[Mid-Season_Invitational/2021|MSI 2021]]. But in the 2022 [[LCK/2022/Summer|LCK Summer]] Split, Gen.G secured their first LCK championship by defeating [[T1]] in the finals with a 3-0 score, earning them the first seed for the [[World_Championship/2022|2022 World Championship]]. At Worlds, Gen.G performed well in the group stage, finishing first, and advanced to the quarter-finals where they beat [[DAMWON Gaming]] in a close 3-2 series. However, in the semi-finals, they faced [[DRX]] and lost the series 1-3. ===King of LCK, Paper Tiger in Internationals (2023)=== In [[LCK/2023/Spring|LCK Spring 2023]], Gen.G once again won the championship by defeating [[T1]] in the finals with a 3-1 score, securing their first seed for the [[Mid-Season_Invitational/2023|Mid-Season Invitational 2023]], alongside [[T1]]. The team finished {{Ordinal|4|sup=yes}} in the Bracket Stage of MSI, after losses to [[T1]] and [[Bilibili Gaming]]. On August 20th, Gen.G emerged victorious in [[LCK/2022/Summer|LCK Summer 2023]], achieving the second three-peat in the history of LCK, while also qualifying for [[World Championship/2023|Worlds]] as LCK's {{Ordinal|1|sup=yes}} seed. In the Swiss Stage, Gen.G were one of the two teams that advanced to the Quarterfinals without dropping a single match. The finalized bracket for the Knockout Stage seemed to favor Gen.G as well, with [[Peyz]] commenting "Luck is on our side."{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/XYgeaW94960|title=Gen.G Quarterfinals Draw Reaction {{!}} Worlds 2023|publisher=[[Gen.G Esports]]|date=2023-10-30|language={{FlagNoLink|kr}} Korean}} However, Gen.G was eliminated by [[BLG]] in the quarterfinals with a 2-3 upset, and Peyz's comment was later interpreted as arrogance. {{Quote |quote=We were told Busan was the Church of Chovy but what's a god to five non-believers? BLG will face Weibo in Semis. |sign=[[Medic]] |source=Worlds 2023 Quarterfinals{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/HzKEBz9oWX8|title="WHAT'S A GOD TO FIVE NON-BELIEVERS"|publisher=LoL Esports|date=2023-11-03}} }} ===First International Crown (2024)=== In [[LCK/2024/Spring|LCK Spring 2024]], Gen.G came out on top of the Group Stage, dropping only one match against [[KT Rolster]]. Their win streak continued, achieving the first 4-peat in the history of LCK.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/LCK/status/1779465354340950523|title=GAME, MATCH, 4-PEAT #LCK CHAMPIONSHIP for @GenG!|author=[[LCK]]|date=2024-04-14}} Their win streak continued in the [[Mid-Season Invitational/2024|MSI]], bringing back the MSI trophy to LCK for the first time in 7 years;{{cite web|url=https://x.com/LCK/status/1792187096720970031|title=BECOME THE CHAMPIONS|author=[[LCK]]|date=2024-05-19}} the first ever international trophy under the name Gen.G. Despite being swept by [[Top Esports|TES]] in the quarterfinals of [[EWC 2024]], Gen.G continued their win streak in the LCK, becoming the first team to qualify for [[World Championship/2024|Worlds]] via the MSI champion seed.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/LCK/status/1813918619711254900|title=Congratulations on the incredible #LCK record, @GenG!|author=[[LCK]]|date=2024-07-27}}{{cite web|url=https://x.com/lolesports/status/1817166758907666741|title=WELCOME TO #WORLDS2024|author=LoL Esports|date=2024-07-27}} ==Gallery== ===Rosters=== GENG Worlds 2020.jpg|Gen.G at [[World_Championship/2020|Worlds 2020]]

Telecom T1}} ==History== ===The Beginning (2012)=== SK Telecom T1 made their debut at [[Intel_Extreme_Masters/Season_VII/Cologne|IEM Cologne]] in 2012, with [[Reapered]], [[H0R0]], [[MighTiLy]], [[UandME]] and [[StarLast]] securing the title for the Korean team with a 2-1 victory against [[Fnatic]]. This team then split up into [[SK Telecom T1 K]] and [[SK Telecom T1 S]]. {{See also|T1/History|l1=History of T1}} ===SKT T1 Dynasty (2015-2017)=== The two teams were merged ahead of 2015 to form a line-up of [[MaRin]], [[Bengi]], [[T0M]], [[Faker]], [[Easyhoon]], [[Bang]], [[Wolf (Korean player)|Wolf]] and [[Piccaboo]]. This team looked like a top challenger right away, winning the [[LCK/2015/Spring|LCK 2015 Spring Split]], before placing 2nd at [[Mid-Season_Invitational/2015|MSI 2015]]. After their [[LCK/2015/Summer|LCK 2015 Summer Split]] championship, SKT won their second [[World_Championship/2015|World Championship]] (first as the merged team), beating countrymates [[KOO Tigers]] 3-1 in the finals. From here on, SK Telecom T1 won 3 titles back to back, the [[Intel_Extreme_Masters/Season_X/World_Championship|IEM Season X World Championship]], [[LCK/2016/Spring|LCK 2016 Spring Split]] and [[Mid-Season_Invitational/2016|MSI 2016]], with [[KT Rolster]] breaking their streak by taking them out 3-2 in the [[LCK/2016/Summer|LCK 2016 Summer Semi-Finals]]. Despite this, [[World Championship/2016|Worlds 2016]] was won by SKT, making them the first team to win back-to-back titles. This performance seemed to carry on in 2017, with them winning [[LCK/2017/Spring|Spring 2017]] and [[Mid-Season_Invitational/2017|MSI 2017]], but they lost in the [[LCK/2017/Summer|LCK 2017 Summer finals]] against [[Longzhu Gaming]], with [[Samsung Galaxy]] taking away their [[World_Championship/2017|Worlds 2017]] title. ===Slumps and Struggles (2018-2021)=== {{Quote |quote=저희 SKT T1은 부진은 있어도 몰락은 없습니다.
[ Us, SKT T1, we may falter, but we never fail. ] |sign=[[kkOma]] |source=LCK Spring 2016 Finals{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/AeWukfKV-y8?t=16321|title=LCK Spring Playoffs - Finals: ROX vs. SKT|publisher=LoL Esports|date=2016-04-23}} }} In [[LCK/2018/Spring|Spring 2018]], [[Untara]] and [[Blank]] joined the team as starting players. This resulted in the team placing {{Ordinal|4|sup=yes}} and making more changes heading into [[LCK/2018/Summer|Summer]]: [[Thal]] replaced [[Untara]], [[Pirean]] joined as secondary midlaner, while [[Effort]] replaced [[Wolf (Korean player)|Wolf]] permanently. This is when SK Telecom T1 missed out on playoffs, placing {{Ordinal|7|sup=yes}} in the regular season. It eventually resulted in them failing to qualify for [[World Championship/2018|Worlds]] too, with a 2-3 loss against [[Gen.G Esports]] in the [[LCK/2018/Regional_Finals|Regional Finals]]. After the disappointing results, SK Telecom T1 rebuilt their team heading into 2019. [[Khan]] joining as a toplaner, [[Clid]] joining as a jungler, [[Teddy]] joining from [[Jin Air Green Wings]] as the new AD Carry and [[Mata]] joining the team from rivals [[KT Rolster]]. This resulted in several titles throughout the year, with them winning the [[LCK/2019/Spring|LCK 2019 Spring Split]] and [[LCK/2019/Summer|LCK 2019 Summer Split]], but coming short at the international events, exiting both in {{Ordinal|3-4|sup=yes}} place. This resulted in another rebuild heading into 2020, with [[Roach]], [[Cuzz]] and [[Effort]] joining the starting line-up. They won the [[LCK/2020/Spring|LCK 2020 Spring Split]], but placed {{Ordinal|5|sup=yes}} in [[LCK/2020/Summer|Summer]] and failed to qualify for [[World Championship/2020|Worlds 2020]] following a [[LCK/2020/Regional_Finals|Regional Finals]] loss against [[Gen.G Esports]]. Trying to build on the young roster, T1 managed to sign Ryu "[[Keria]]" Min-seok who had just been released from [[DRX]], who would be replacing [[Effort]] who ended up leaving for [[SANDBOX Gaming]] later that year. This roster would place {{Ordinal|4|sup=yes}} in [[LCK/2021/Spring|Spring 2021]], with a lot of criticism coming T1's way for their extreme amount of player switching throughout the regular season. In [[LCK/2021/Summer|Summer 2021]], coaches [[Daeny]] and [[Zefa]] were released from the team in the middle of the split, with [[Stardust (Korean player)|Stardust]] and [[Moment]] joining as temporary coaches. They placed second in the Summer split, losing against [[DAMWON Gaming]] in the finals, but managed to secure a ticket to [[World Championship|Worlds 2021]] with a 3-2 win against [[Hanwha Life Esports]] in the [[LCK/2021/Regional_Finals|Regional Finals]]. Following T1's {{Ordinal|3-4|sup=yes}} place finish at [[World Championship/2021|Worlds 2021]], the team parted ways with [[Canna]], [[Ellim]], [[Cuzz]], [[Clozer]], [[Teddy]] and [[Hoit]]. ===The Beginning of ZOFGK Roster (2022)=== T1 promoted [[Zeus]] to the starting roster, forming the [[Zeus]]-[[Oner]]-[[Faker]]-[[Gumayusi]]-[[Keria]] (ZOFGK) roster. T1 managed to become the first [[LCK]] team to ever go undefeated in the regular season, beating their own [[LCK/2015/Summer|LCK Summer 2015]] record, where they finished with a 17-1 record. After winning the [[LCK/2022/Spring|Spring 2022]] 3-1 over [[Gen.G Esports]], the team would go to [[Mid-Season Invitational/2022|MSI 2022]] making it to the knockout stage with a 7-3 record in the rumble stage qualifying second. The team would face [[G2]], a team that went 1-1 with in the rumble stage but would clean sweep them in a 3-0 series. Their next opponent was [[Royal Never Give Up]] where T1 would take blows with them and eventually would go to game 5 where T1 lost out and saw [[Royal Never Give Up]] become champions in Korea. The [[LCK/2022/Summer|Summer Split]] saw T1 end the group stage as {{Ordinal|2|sup=yes}} place with a 15-3 record. T1 would stop the reverse sweep of [[DAMWON Gaming]] winning the series 3-2 and once again found themselves against [[Gen.G Esports]]; this time getting swept in the finals losing 3-0. At [[World Championship/2022|Worlds 2022]] they found themselves in a group with [[EDward Gaming]], [[Cloud9]] and [[Fnatic]]. They made it out of groups as the first seed 5-1. In the quaterfinals they would face [[Royal Never Give Up]] getting their revenge T1 would sweep the LPL team winning 3-0. The next oppnent was the LPL's first seed [[JD Gaming]]. T1 would drop the first game but ultimately won 3-1. In the finals they would face [[DRX]]. T1 would take the lead 2-1 but then [[DRX]] would eventually win the series 3-2. Following T1's {{Ordinal|2|sup=yes}} place finish they decided to keep the same ZOFGK roster for the 2023 season. ===Reignition of SKT Legacy (2023)=== In 2023, T1 had a strong start in the [[LCK/2023/Spring|LCK 2023 Spring Split]] with a 17-1 record but lost the Grand Final to [[Gen.G Esports]]. Despite this, they directly qualified for the [[Mid-Season Invitational/2023|MSI 2023]] playoffs, where they had a series of victories and defeats, eventually losing to [[Bilibili Gaming]] in the Lower Bracket Final. One month after the start of the [[LCK/2023/Summer|Summer Split]], [[Faker]] was temporarily benched due to an injury, with [[Poby]] standing in for Faker's position. Despite having a tough 1-7 record during one month of Faker's absence, and despite [[Bengi]]'s resignation as the head coach that happened mid-season, they managed to come back up and ended the regular season {{Ordinal|5|sup=yes}} with a 9-9 record. They had a series of wins in the playoffs but were swept by [[Gen.G Esports]] in the Grand Final. Still, they qualified for [[World Championship/2023|Worlds 2023]] as LCK's {{Ordinal|2|sup=yes}} seed with the accumulated points. T1 made their way through the Swiss stage with a 3-1 record, only dropping a match against [[Gen.G Esports|Gen.G]]. After sweeping [[BLG]] 2-0 in their last match of Swiss Stage, they first had to face of against [[LNG Esports]] from the [[LPL]]. As they entered the last quarterfinals match, after the fall of all other LCK teams in Worlds, T1 had become the "LCK's final hope"{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/RUWVgBceVdI|title=LNG vs T1 {{!}} SCOUT VS FAKER {{!}} Quarterfinals Day 4 Tease {{!}} Worlds 2023|author=|publisher=LoL Esports|date=2023-11-05}} by being the only team remaining in Worlds outside of the LPL. T1 was were able to sweep 3-0 against LNG. {{Quote |quote=And even as every other LCK team falls away, FAKER stays standing. T1 stays standing! The last light of the LCK burns bright at Busan, as they head to the semifinals! |sign=[[Drakos]] |source=Worlds 2023 Quarterfinals Day 4{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/I8DcHjbKcII?t=2276|title=LNG vs. T1 - Game 3 {{!}} KNOCKOUTS Stage {{!}} 2023 Worlds {{!}} LNG Esports vs T1 (2023)|publisher=LoL Esports VODs and Highlights|date=2023-11-05}} }} Their next opponent was [[JD Gaming]], a team that was looking to complete their "Golden Road" and were seen as the favourites to win the tournament. However, T1 was able to come out on top in the series with a 3-1 upset. {{Quote |quote=It is not LPL versus LCK, it is T1 versus the LPL! And they like those odds, as they move to Finals! |sign=[[Drakos]] |source=Worlds 2023 Semifinals{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/yV8NwMgqcD4&t=2714|title=JDG vs. T1 - Game 4 {{!}} SEMIFINALS Stage {{!}} 2023 Worlds {{!}} JDG Intel Esports Club vs T1 (2023)|author=|publisher=LoL Esports|date=2023-11-12}} }} With their victory, T1 entered their sixth World Finals; this time being faced with [[Weibo Gaming]]. T1 dominated the series and swept the final LPL team 3-0, becoming the first team to win 4 Worlds titles. {{Quote |quote=It was 7 years since their last, and a decade since their first; the SKT legacy has been reignited! T1 will be your 2023 WORLD CHAMPIONS! |sign=[[Atlus]] |source=Worlds 2023 Grand Final{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/LmD_ShTbIq0?t=2240|title=WBG vs. T1 - Game 3 {{!}} FINALS Stage {{!}} 2023 Worlds {{!}} Weibo Gaming vs T1 (2023)|author=|publisher=LoL Esports VODs and Highlights|date=2023-11-19}} }} Shortly after the team's victory, contracts of players [[Gumayusi]], [[Keria]], and [[Zeus]] were renewed as they were due to expire after Worlds. The team also announced the return of [[kkOma]] as the head coach. ===The New T1 Empire (2024)=== With the same ZOFGK roster, T1 started off the year strong, by only dropping a single match against [[Gen.G Esports|Gen.G]] in the first round of [[LCK/2024/Spring|Spring]] regular season. At the same time, T1 started getting [[wikipedia:Denial-of-service attack#Distributed DoS|distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks]], which later affected the entire league. This resulted in extended game pauses and switching to pre-recorded streams in LCK. T1 was severely affected by the attacks, affecting their practices and their overall form.{{cite web|url=https://www.inven.co.kr/webzine/news/?news=294288|title=T1 김정균 감독 "디도스 피해 심각...연습도 쉽지 않다"|trans_title=T1 Head Coach Kim Jeong-gyun "The damage from DDoS is serious... Doing practices is not easy"|language={{FlagNoLink|kr}} Korean|author=김홍제|publisher=INVEN}} Although they finished second in the regular season, they were swept 0-3 by [[HLE]], with Faker admitting that not being able to practice in solo ranked affected them heavily.{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/ylzHNKBrcZo|title=0대 3 패배 T1 페이커 "다른 팀에 비해 솔로랭크 연습 못한 영향 있었다"|trans_title=T1 Faker after 0-3 loss "Not being able to practice with solo ranked compared to other teams affected us"|language={{FlagNoLink|kr}} Korean|publisher=fomos esports}} Despite the challenges, T1 managed to sweep [[Dplus]] 3-0 in the lower bracket, then took revenge on [[HLE]] with a 3-1 win in the [[Match:ID LCK24SprPO R03-M002|Lower Bracket Final]], securing their spot in the [[Mid-Season Invitational/2024|MSI]].
